en: The Sūtra on the Inconceivable Realm of Supernatural Powers Spoken by the Buddha, Volume One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master from the Western Heaven, Chao Feng Da Fu, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
Translated by the Dharma Master Śīladhara, recipient of the purple robe and subject of the Imperial Court, by imperial decree. Thus have I heard:

At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in the Palace of the Bodhisattva Dharmadhātu-prabhāsa, together with a great assembly of five hundred thousand bhikṣus. All were arhats whose outflows were exhausted and who were free from all remaining afflictions; they dwelt in tranquility, their minds well-liberated and their wisdom well-liberated. Like great dragon kings, they had accomplished what was to be done, laid down their heavy burdens, attained the great benefit of supreme excellence, and had completely severed all fetters of existence. Their right knowledge was unimpeded, their minds were perfectly serene, and they were fully endowed with supernormal powers.

Furthermore, there was an assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who had all attained the stage of non-retrogression and were in their final birth before attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; they were all firmly established in the boundless supernatural transformations of the Tathāgatas and in the unattached, wondrous practices empowered by bodhi.

All sentient beings possess vast love and joy; abiding in right mindfulness and wisdom, they enter universal knowledge and are endowed with impartial conduct. Having accomplished an immeasurable mass of meritorious qualities, they have realized the Tathāgata’s dharma-gate of equality, turned the wondrous wheel of Dharma, and are able to skillfully instruct boundless assemblies of disciples, having already attained all the merits of pure dharmas.

They thoroughly know the mentalities of all sentient beings and discern the sharpness or dullness of their faculties; having reached the further shore of supreme mastery and accomplished all wholesome dharmas in their perfection, they have come from worlds in other directions to assemble at this gathering, having fully completed all the works of the Buddhas.
Their names were:

the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantaketu, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantagati, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantaśraddha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantanetra, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabodhi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantaprabha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantagandha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantamati-ghoṣa, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantāloka, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantasmṛti, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantajñānaketu, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantālambanadarśin, and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharmadhātu-samantaprabha; together with these twelve thousand others.
Furthermore, there was a multitude of devaputras, namely:

the devaputra Jñānaketu, the devaputra Samantakusumaketu, the devaputra Samantaprabha, the devaputra Ratnaśikhin, and the devaputra Ratnasaṃcayamaṇiśikhara; together with these ten thousand devaputras, they were all assembled.
All these sons of the gods, who had already planted various roots of goodness under past Buddhas, gathered for this assembly.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the samādhi of Universal Radiance; emerging from this samādhi, he immediately emitted a vast light that illuminated the trichiliocosm and shone universally upon all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions.

At that time, all sentient beings throughout these worlds who were touched by the light all resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; those who had already resolved their minds all came to dwell securely in the stage of non-retrogression.

At that time, in all the Buddha-fields throughout the worlds of the ten directions, the various Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, together with their retinues of attendant bodhisattvas, having seen this light, each addressed their respective Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
"Now this radiance shines universally upon the world; what are its causes and conditions, and what is this divine power?
Thereupon, each of those Buddhas said:
"O sons of good family!..."

"You should know that there is a world named Sahā, where the Buddha is called Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. He is currently assembled together with a great multitude of Bodhisattvas, desiring to proclaim the True Dharma of the inconceivable realm; it is for this reason that light shines everywhere."
At that time, those who were the personal attendants of each of those Buddhas addressed their respective Buddhas, saying:
"World-Honored One!

We now wish to go to that Sahā world to behold, pay homage to, and revere the Tathāgata Śākyamuni; to rejoice in and listen to the true Dharma of the inconceivable realm; and to see the multitude of bodhisattvas there."
Then that Tathāgata addressed each of his attendants, saying:
"You may go; now is the very time to do as you wish."

At that time, all those who served as close attendants to the Buddhas in every Buddha-field throughout the ten directions each manifested various transformations through their bodhisattva supernormal powers; accompanied by countless devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and others, they came with reverent entourage to the place where Śākyamuni Buddha was.
When these bodhisattvas had arrived at the Buddha’s assembly, they bowed their heads in earnest reverence at the feet of the World-Honored One and all spoke thus:
“World-Honored One, Tathāgata Śākyamuni!

Having heard the name of this inconceivable realm of the True Dharma, we desire to rejoice in it, listen to its exposition, and receive it; furthermore, we wish to see the Buddha, the World-Honored One, to gaze upon him with reverence and pay our respects, as well as to see this great assembly of bodhisattvas. For these reasons, we have come to this Sahā world.
At that time, in the eastern world-system of Mahāratna, within the Buddha-field of Ratnaketu, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī, who dwelt there, had this thought:

"Now, in that western Sahā world, within the Buddha-field of Śākyamuni, there is a great assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas from worlds in the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, all gathered together to listen to that Buddha’s teaching of the True Dharma of the inconceivable realm."
I should now likewise go to that assembly to pay homage to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, who is near;
there I shall rejoice in hearing and receiving that Dharma-gate, and behold those bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Why is this? Throughout all the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, wherever there are assemblies for the benefit of beings, I go to them all without exception.

Furthermore, I have never before seen such assemblies of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas preaching the Dharma as I do today; in those Buddha-fields, there are such immeasurable and boundless great assemblies of Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas. I observe that such a sight is extremely rare, and to see or hear it is even more difficult. For this reason, I too ought now to go there.
At that time, after the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī had formed this thought, he addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, saying:

"Maitreya, you should know that within the realm of the present World-Honored One Śākyamuni Buddha, there is a vast assembly of countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, who are listening to and receiving the teaching of the sublime Dharma of the inconceivable realm. We should now go together to pay our respects to the World-Honored One and to see those great Bodhisattva Sattvas!"
"Why is this? It is an exceedingly rare occurrence for the great bodhisattvas of the worlds of the ten directions to assemble together in one place.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying:
"You should now go yourself to that Buddha's assembly; it is not for me to go there.
Why is this? Because it is extremely difficult."

The great bodhisattvas in that Buddha’s assembly have all attained the gates of dhāraṇī; they abide in non-attached wisdom and are endowed with all wholesome dharmas. Even if one were to see or hear them in that gathering, I am unable to perceive any signs of them.
Mañjuśrī! You should know this now:
if one perceives the Tathāgata by means of his form-body (rūpakāya), there is in fact nothing to be seen; therefore, I am currently unable to see him.

If one perceives the Tathāgata by means of his dharma-body (dharmakāya), the dharma-body is itself the dharma-nature (dharmatā). Within the dharma-nature, there is neither seeing nor hearing, no making of offerings, no gazing upon or prostrating to, and no cognitive apprehension.
The Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī said:
"You should now follow him to that place to make offerings to the Tathāgata.
The Bodhisattva Maitreya said:
"No, Mañjuśrī! It was not I who made offerings to the Tathāgata."
Why is this? Because there is no Tathāgata who can perform an offering.
The Tathāgata is precisely the dharma of true suchness (tathatā); within the dharma of true suchness there are no dual characteristics, and the dharma of true suchness is itself the Tathāgata.
The Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī asked:
"Regarding this very non-dual characteristic, how would you explain it?
Maitreya replied:
“Mañjuśrī! To speak of the single nature and the manifold nature of afflictions is called duality;
if one realizes that the single nature is itself the manifold, this is the non-dual Dharma.”
If one gives rise to discrimination, thinking "this is affliction" and "this is supramundane," such a view constitutes dualistic characteristics.
Furthermore, if one discriminates, thinking "this is the observance of precepts" and "this is not the observance of precepts";
or "this is the Dharma of the Śrāvakas" and "this is the Dharma of the Pratyekabuddhas"; [one likewise falls into dualism].
"This is giving; this is not giving.
This is the right path; this is the wrong path.
This is a srotāpanna, a sakṛdāgāmin, an anāgāmin, or an arhat; this is a pratyekabuddha; this is a bodhisattva; this is a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
"This dharma is subject to cessation; this dharma possesses ideation;
this dharma is determinate; this is indeterminate;
this dharma is known by wisdom; this dharma is cognized by consciousness."
"This is the path of awakening;
this is the path to nirvāṇa"—to make such distinctions is to dwell in dualistic signs (*dvaya-nimitta*), and within these dualistic signs, one follows the fluctuations of consciousness (*vijñāna*).
If one can refrain from giving rise to such signs, that is the non-dual dharma (*advaya-dharma*).

Mañjuśrī! Even if I were to speak of this non-dual dharma for an eon, or until the end of an eon, even with such eloquence and wisdom, I could not exhaustively explain it, nor could I know its ultimate limit.
"Why is this? Because all those phenomena are devoid of manifold natures; whether in the middle or at the extremes, they are neither visible nor obtainable.
Thus spoke the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.
“Magnificent, Maitreya!
Because you have already realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti), you speak thus. It is so, it is so!”
"Even if I were to spend an eon, or even the end of an eon, speaking of this non-dual Dharma, it could not be fully exhausted by the power of eloquence or wisdom.
Maitreya Bodhisattva said, "Mañjuśrī!"
"Do not give rise to the notion of existence regarding words and letters; all those dharmas are free from all words and letters. This is the mark of non-arising, and it is also without movement.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī addressed all the bodhisattvas within that buddha-field, saying:
"Sons of good family!

"You all should now go together to that buddha-field of the World-Honored One Śākyamuni Buddha to pay homage to that Buddha, and to see the hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas, and to rejoice in and listen to the inconceivable realm of the True Dharma."
At that time, there was a bodhisattva named Prajñākūṭadhvajarāja who addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying:
“The Tathāgata cannot possibly be seen; for what reason do you now say, ‘I command you all to go and see the Buddha, the Tathāgata’?”
What is it that makes the Tathāgata visible?
Furthermore, for what reason is he called "Tathāgata"? Why is this so?
The Tathāgata cannot be apprehended as past, future, or present.
All those dharmas likewise do not belong to the three periods of time, for they are entirely empty; within these empty dharmas, there is no one who can see.
As the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī has said:
"The Tathāgata has something seen. How, then, does he see that Buddha-Tathāgata?
By what eye can he be observed?
If one were able to perceive with the fleshly eye, the fleshly eye would be empty, and within emptiness there is nothing to be seen;
if one perceives the Tathāgata with the divine eye, the divine eye likewise involves the notion of attainment;
if it is not perceived by means of the eyes, how can it be called "seeing"?
"Therefore, we are unable to go at this time.
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva said, "Noble sons!"
If you now abide in the dharma of inequality and speak thus, you will be unable to see the Buddha, the Tathāgata, nor will you be making an offering to him.

If you now abide in the mark of non-attachment and speak according to reality, you will indeed see the Buddha, the Tathāgata; you will have a destination and you will be able to make offerings, because you do not cling to the marks of any words, yet you also do not depart from the marks of all words.
That intrinsic nature is empty; therefore, within the dharma of equality, I speak thus:
"Because all Tathāgatas are fundamentally pure, the Tathāgata likewise does not move or shift."
“You all should now go there if you abide in a mind of patience;
you should also go there if you do not abide in a mind of patience.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī thus repeatedly and skillfully explained this to the bodhisattvas. Through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, that assembly of bodhisattvas immediately attained non-abiding with respect to all phenomena.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī again had this thought:
"I should not go alone now to that Sahā world. Why is this?"
"In that world, all sentient beings who have committed unwholesome deeds see little and hear little, and thus do not give rise to pure faith.

I shall now manifest various physical forms and rare wonders so as to go there, causing all those beings to give rise to faith and experience what they have never had before, thereby enabling them to obtain vast and great benefits."

Immediately, after Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva had formed this thought, he entered the *vimalasamantaprabha-samādhi*. Within that samādhi, he saw himself surrounded by countless hundreds of thousands of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, with all the Great Brahmā Kings and Śakra Devendra each holding precious whisks, standing in attendance at his left and right.

At that time, from each and every pore of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, there emerged celestial lotuses as large as chariot wheels; within each lotus sat a Buddha, the World-Honored One, in the full lotus posture, and each World-Honored One held a precious lotus flower.
At that time, all sentient beings within the trichiliocosm attained great bliss.

The Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī immediately perceived all sentient beings, and those sentient beings likewise perceived the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī; they all became non-retrogressive from the mind set upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, having seen these signs, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī emerged from samādhi. Having come from the great jewel Buddha-field in the eastern direction to this Sahā world, he manifested such supernatural transformations in every Buddha-field through which he passed, universally causing all beings to obtain great benefit.
In those various Buddha-fields, they all see the Tathāgatas holding precious lotus flowers, each preaching the Dharma for those sentient beings;
or they see the Buddha-fields where hell-dwellers currently undergoing suffering are all liberated from their pain through the Buddha’s salvation;
and those in the realms of animals and hungry ghosts who are tormented by extreme suffering as they devour one another are likewise all freed from their suffering.
Even unto those beings within the realm of Yama who were currently undergoing all manner of suffering and affliction, they saw the Buddha and he preached the Dharma to each according to their needs.
Each and every one of these beings was able to distance themselves from suffering and affliction, and each gave rise to the mind set upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
In some buddha-fields, one may see the Tathāgata extensively preaching the Dharma as appropriate for all the hosts of asuras, so that each of them attains the transformation of their asura body.

In some buddha-fields, one may see the Tathāgata dwelling within the sphere of the supernatural powers of Mañjuśrī, preaching the Dharma as appropriate for the great kṣatriya clans, the great brahmin clans, and the great householder clans, so that each obtains benefit; or he may preach the Dharma as appropriate for the hosts of devaputras of the Cāturmahārājika heaven, saying to those devaputras:
"You should know that all conditioned phenomena are entirely impermanent; do not give rise to the thought that they are ultimate dharmas."
All who hear this Dharma shall obtain benefit.

In certain buddha-fields, one may see the Tathāgata dwelling within the sphere of Mañjuśrī’s supernatural powers, teaching the Dharma as appropriate to the assembly of devaputras, such as Śakra, the Lord of the Thirty-three Heavens.
He further said:
"All conditioned phenomena are impermanent and are not ultimate dharmas; those who possess wisdom should know them as they truly are, and should not conceive of them as being ultimate."
All who hear this Dharma obtain benefit.

In some buddha-fields, one may see the Tathāgata dwelling within the sphere of Mañjuśrī’s supernatural powers, preaching the Dharma as appropriate for the hosts of devaputras of the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, the Brahmakāyika Heaven, the Brahmapurohita Heaven, the Mahābrahmā Heaven, and so on, up to the hosts of devaputras of the Akaniṣṭha Heaven; all who hear the Dharma thus preached obtain benefit.

In some instances, he saw the Tathāgata abiding in the sphere of the supernatural powers of Mañjuśrī, preaching the Dharma as appropriate for the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the first bhūmi;

or for those of the second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, or tenth bhūmi; or for the great assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are in their final birth (*ekajātipratibaddha*) and destined to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. To each, he preached the essentials of the Dharma as was fitting, causing them to advance and dwell in non-retrogression, even universally leading them to perfect and abide in the realm of Great Nirvāṇa.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī manifested such various supernatural transformations. In all the Buddha-fields he passed through, every sentient being who beheld these signs gave rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Five hundred bhikṣus attained the exhaustion of all outflows and their minds were well-liberated; eight thousand bodhisattvas attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpāda-dharma-kṣānti*); and ten thousand devaputras, free from dust and defilement, attained the purity of the Dharma-eye.
At that moment, the bodhisattvas who had received these benefits spoke in unison with a single voice, uttering these verses:
“Beholding these miraculous transformations, All are fulfilled in ways never before seen;
Within the sphere of the Honored Mañjuśrī, All sentient beings obtain benefit.”

At that time, the assembly of bodhisattvas who had gathered from the buddha-fields of the ten directions each witnessed such great and rare wonders through their own supernormal powers. They addressed the World-Honored One, Śākyamuni Buddha, saying:
"What supernatural power has manifested this light that universally illuminates this trichiliocosm and these rare wonders?"
"We pray that the Buddha, the World-Honored One, will explain this for us.
The Buddha addressed the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, saying:
"Good sons!..."

"You should know that there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Mañjuśrī, who dwells in non-retrogression and has already received empowerment; he is coming from the east, wishing to enter this assembly, and it is through his supernormal powers that these auspicious signs have appeared."
Furthermore, noble son!
If anyone should hear the name of that Mañjuśrī, they shall all abide in the mind of non-retrogression; how much more difficult is it, then, to actually behold him!

At that time, while the World-Honored One Śākyamuni Buddha was speaking thus to the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, by means of his supernormal powers, entered the assembly of the Buddha. Having arrived at the assembly, he prostrated himself with his head to the ground before the feet of the World-Honored One and addressed the Buddha:
"World-Honored One Śākyamuni Buddha!"
Are you free from illness and affliction? Are you physically light, well-adjusted, and at ease?
I have come from the world-system of Mahāratna in the eastern direction, the Buddha-field of Ratnadhvaja, to this assembly to pay homage to the World-Honored One and to hear the True Dharma.
At that time, the celestial son Samantakusumaketu rose from his seat within the great assembly and approached the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What dharmas should the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate so that they may achieve the most supreme, profound eloquence and wisdom, as well as the miraculous activities of Mañjuśrī?”
The Buddha addressed the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu, saying:
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to accomplish such superior activities of supernormal powers, they should be fully endowed with four dharma-gates."
What are the four?
First, to joyfully listen to and receive the profound Dharma.
Second, to extensively expound the profound Dharma for others.
Third, to inquire about the meaning of the Dharma as it is heard.
Fourth, having heard it, to believe and understand it and practice accordingly.
These are the four kinds.
Furthermore, there are four dharmas that one should fully possess. What are these four?
First, to maintain with certainty and retain all the sūtras and teachings spoken by the Buddha-Tathāgata.
Second, to delight in and cultivate all the teachings of the sūtras;
third, to remember and not forget all the teachings of the sūtras;
fourth, to extensively explain and propagate all the teachings of the sūtras.
These are the four kinds.
Furthermore, there are four other dharmas that should be fully possessed. What are these four?
First, to listen to and receive the true Dharma with earnest attention.
Second, to conceive a sense of reverence toward the teacher who expounds the Dharma.
Third, to serve and attend upon those who uphold the Dharma with respect, without becoming weary or regressing.
Fourth, one should always praise the Dharma teacher and remain free from weariness for a long time.
These are the four kinds.
Furthermore, there are four other dharmas that should be fully possessed.
What are the four?
They are: one should always give rise to the four minds.
First, a mind of equanimity;
second, a supple mind;
third, an untiring mind.
The fourth is a mind free from poison.
These are the four kinds.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices these four dharma-gates according to their cultivation, they will immediately attain such supreme activities of supernatural transformations and further achieve wisdom and eloquence.

At that time, when the World-Honored One had spoken these four Dharma-gates, five thousand bodhisattvas attained the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), and four thousand devaputras were freed from dust and defilement, attaining the pure Dharma-eye (*dharma-cakṣur-viśuddhi*).
Having obtained these benefits, the assembly of bodhisattvas and devaputras all spoke thus:

"May all sentient beings universally attain dwelling within the realm of all Buddhas, give rise to profound faith and understanding toward the gateways of the True Dharma, and remember, retain, and uphold the True Dharma they hear. In future ages, may they attain great supernormal powers like those of Mañjuśrī, and exercise sovereign mastery over transformations within all Buddha-fields."
At that time, the devaputra Samantakusumaketu addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying:
"From what place has the Bodhisattva come to this assembly of the Buddha?
What is the name of the buddha-field where you dwell?"
"What is the name of the Tathāgata who performed this transformation?
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī said to the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu:
"Do not speak in such a manner."
“Having come from somewhere. Why is this?
Your Majesty, you should know that the dharma-realm neither comes nor goes; furthermore, it has no movement and no abiding, being entirely free from attachment.
That nature of the dharma-realm is free from doubt and devoid of all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*).
O Son of Heaven!
If one speaks of coming, going, or abiding, these are the dharmas of conceptual proliferation.

At that time, the celestial son Samantakusumaketu and the great assembly, having heard this Dharma taught by the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, immediately each marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence and, with one voice, spoke these verses:
"Most supreme and rare, O Mañjuśrī!
Born from the Buddha, the World-Honored One;
these dharma-gates endowed with supernormal powers bring benefit to all who hear or behold them.
Now this Great Being manifests these various marks and proclaims the profound and subtle Dharma.
I rejoice that I have been able to see and hear this; today we all obtain great benefit.
In the past we heard of the Great Beings of Renown; today we behold their wondrous physical forms and supernormal powers.
These Bodhisattvas are the radiance of the Great Dharma, manifesting all the teachings of the Buddhas.
Having already perfected all practices, adorned with the supreme raiment of shame and modesty;
Mañjuśrī, who brings benefit to self and others, possesses inconceivable and most excellent virtues.
The Bodhisattva is like a father to the world, universally gathering all beings as those to whom they may turn;
revealing the gateway of the skillful means to nirvāṇa, he causes all sentient beings to reach the other shore.
The Bodhisattva is like a great lion; with a single sound, he can shatter all external doctrines.
The merits of the True Dharma are already perfected, and all defiled phenomena are rendered pure.
The Bodhisattva is like the earth of the world, Capable of universally producing all wholesome dharmas;
Furthermore, he is the supreme Great King of Physicians, Able to rescue sentient beings from the suffering of all diseases.
The Bodhisattva is like the moon, great in its coolness, Causing all torments of heat to become pure;
Furthermore, like the sun, its light is fiercely blazing, Universally illuminating all samādhis.
The Bodhisattva, the great-benefactor and great guide, leads and shows sentient beings the path to bodhi;
constantly giving rise to a vast mind of loving-kindness and compassion, he rescues and delivers sentient beings from the sufferings of the evil realms.
The Bodhisattva is always a refuge for all, discerning the minds of every sentient being;
through the sublime gateway of the wisdom of all-knowledge, he universally bestows liberation upon all beings.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu and the great assembly, saying:
"So it is, so it is. It is as you have said; the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī possesses such merit."
The Sūtra on the Inconceivable Realm of Supernormal Powers Spoken by the Buddha, Volume One;
The Sūtra on the Inconceivable Realm of Supernormal Powers Spoken by the Buddha, Volume Two.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlagupta, Dharma-transmitting Master and Imperially Conferred Purple Robe, Court Official of the Fourth Rank (Chao Feng Da Fu) and Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (Shi Guang Lu Qing), under imperial decree. At that time, the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
"O Son of Heaven, how long has this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī now been resolved upon awakening?
The Buddha said:
"Son of Heaven!"
"O Son of Heaven! This Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī has already resolved upon bodhicitta more than immeasurable and boundless kalpas ago, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Now, for your sake and that of this great assembly, I shall briefly explain one instance of it."
At that time, the devaputra Samantakusumaketu addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We pray that you will, for the sake of us and this entire assembly, proclaim the teaching in accordance with the truth.”
The Buddha said,
“Son of Heaven! In the past,
as many eons ago as there are atoms of dust, at that time in this Sahā world there was a Buddha named Samantadarśana-viśuddhasvararāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who appeared in the world.”
Within that Buddha’s Dharma, there was a bhikṣu named Viśuddhasvara who, having gone forth in that Dharma, cultivated the path and attained the five supernormal powers.

For forty-two thousand years, that bhikṣu made offerings to that Buddha with various kinds of incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, and manifold exquisite requisites; by planting these roots of goodness, he gave rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
"Son of Heaven!
What do you think? Was the bhikṣu Pure Sound at that time someone else?
He was none other than the present Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī."

"You all should know that this Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī has, in the presence of immeasurable and boundless Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, generated the mind of enlightenment; he has delivered beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, establishing them in the fruits of srotāpanna, sakṛdāgāmin, anāgāmin, and arhat;
he has delivered beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, establishing them in the fruit of pratyekabuddha;
and he has delivered beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, establishing them from the first bhūmi up to the tenth bhūmi."
In this way, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī extensively plants various roots of goodness and accomplishes wholesome dharmas.
"Furthermore, O Son of Heaven!
Suppose there were someone who offered as much of the seven treasures as would fill a trichiliocosm to the Tathāgata; the merit obtained by that person would be exceedingly great."

Furthermore, if there should be anyone who hears the name of this Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī and respectfully upholds it, or even rejoices in it and recites it with mindfulness, one should know that this person’s merit is far greater than that.
Furthermore, O Son of Heaven!
If all sentient beings within the trichiliocosm were each to attain the fruit of a Srotāpanna up to that of an Arhat, the merit gained by those people would be exceedingly great;
yet if there were another person who, upon hearing the name of this Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, were able to receive and uphold it, their merit would be even greater than that.

Furthermore, if every single sentient being within the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-system were to attain the fruit of a pratyekabuddha, the merit gained by those people would be exceedingly great;
yet if there were another person who, upon hearing the name of this Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, were able to receive and uphold it, their merit would be even greater than that.

Why is this? If there is one person who praises and upholds the names of all the Buddhas, and another person who praises and upholds the name of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, the merit obtained by these two individuals is equal and without distinction.

At that time, having heard these words spoken by the Buddha, the World-Honored One, the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu, together with forty thousand devaputras, joined their palms in reverent homage and spoke thus:
"Excellent, O Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva!"
"Excellent, excellent!
We sincerely take refuge in you and pay homage to you with our heads bowed.
When those devaputras uttered these words, their voices resounded throughout the entire trichiliocosm, heard from afar by all.
At that time, having heard this sound, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana approached the Buddha and addressed him, saying:
"World-Honored One!
Now throughout this trichiliocosm, everyone hears this sound of praise."
"By what spiritual power has this rare and inconceivable phenomenon been manifested?
The Buddha addressed Mahāmaudgalyāyana, saying:

"You should now know that this is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī—already established in non-retrogression and clad in the great armor, a most supreme Great Being—who is present in this assembly. It is because the sons of the gods and others here praise his name that his voice is heard throughout the trichiliocosm."
Mahāmaudgalyāyana!
If there is anyone who, in whatever place they may be, praises and upholds the name of this Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, at that very moment the entire trichiliocosm will tremble universally.
At that time, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"It is marvelous, World-Honored One!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such inconceivable deeds; donning the great armor of courageous and diligent effort, he brings sentient beings to maturity and fulfills all the Buddha-dharmas."
“World-Honored One!
If a person possesses only meager roots of goodness, they will not be able to thus fulfill and perfect the Dharma of a Great Bodhisattva.

When the World-Honored One was preaching this Dharma for Mahāmaudgalyāyana, a great jewel lotus suddenly appeared, filling the entire Sahā world. Each individual lotus was as large as a chariot wheel; each flower possessed various colors and fragrances, adorned with nets of exquisite jewels. From among these flowers, one lotus emerged most prominently, lofty, radiant, and magnificent, such that the entire assembly beheld it.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, seeing that these exquisite and magnificent lotuses had suddenly appeared, addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One,
why has such a sign appeared at the beginning of this assembly?"
The Buddha said, “Ānanda!

You should now observe that before long, sixty thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas will come to this assembly from the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Śrīguṇarāja in the world-system Samantaprabhāsa, each sitting cross-legged upon his own precious lotus flower.”
Among those lotuses, the one that is most exalted and prominent shall have a bodhisattva named Samantāloka-garbha seated upon it in the full-lotus posture.
Because these bodhisattvas wish to manifest in mid-air, they first display this sign of the precious lotus.

At that time, all the bodhisattvas and the entire great assembly in the congregation together praised this as something never before experienced; each joined their palms and prostrated toward the sky.
At that time, in the midst of the void, there were Brahmā Kings and Śakras holding precious lotus flowers, surrounding the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantaprabhāsa-garbha.
Then this Bodhisattva and all the great beings immediately leaped into the air to a height of seven *tāla* trees, and the entire assembly beheld them all.
At that time, the bodhisattvas rained down various precious flowers from the sky—of manifold colors and fragrances, most exquisite and supreme—to make offerings to the Buddha.
Having made this floral offering, a voice issued forth from the midst of the void:
"World-Honored One!..."
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śrīguṇarāja inquires after the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni:
Are you free from illness and affliction? Are you light and at ease, experiencing great happiness, and is your physical strength secure?
The Tathāgata Śrīguṇarāja asked this question:
"Now, sixty thousand bodhisattvas mahāsattvas, including the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantaprabhāgarbha and others, have come together to this place to pay homage to the World-Honored One."
"Rejoice in hearing and receiving this inconceivable realm of the True Dharma.

When these words had resounded from the sky, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantaprabhāgarbha and all the other Bodhisattvas immediately descended one by one from the air. Having bowed their heads to the ground at the Buddha’s feet, they stood before him.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing this matter, intentionally asked again:
"Universal Illumination Treasury Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva and all you sons of good family!
For what reason have you now come here?"
The Bodhisattva Samantaprabhāgarbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

In the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Śrīguṇarāja within the world-system of Universal Radiance, we have heard that in this Sahā world, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, has gathered together with various bodhisattva mahāsattvas to proclaim the True Dharma of the inconceivable realm.”
"We have come here for this reason: we wish to see the World-Honored One and hear the True Dharma.
At that time, the Venerable Mahākāśyapa stepped forward from within the great assembly and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
Is the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Śrīguṇarājendra in the world-system Samantaprabhā not far from this Buddha-field?
For what reason have these great beings been able to arrive here so swiftly in such a short time?
The Bodhisattva Samantaprabhāgarbha said to Mahākāśyapa:
"Venerable One!
Even if you were to travel to that world by means of your own supernormal powers and meditative concentration, you would not reach it even when your lifespan has come to an end."
"Therefore, you should know that the world of that Buddha is distant from here by such a measure.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Mahākāśyapa, saying:

"From this world, passing through as many Buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in sixty Ganges Rivers, one arrives at the World of Universal Radiance; these bodhisattvas, by means of their most supreme and great supernormal powers, are able to reach it with speed."
At that time, the Venerable Mahākāśyapa addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I now wish to go to that world.”
The Bodhisattva Samantāloka-garbha then asked the Venerable Mahākāśyapa:
"Venerable One, how is it that you have any movement or fluctuation regarding thoughts of coming and going?
Kāśyapa!"
In what dharma do you perceive coming and going?
Do you say that the dharma of form has coming and going?
Or that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness have coming and going?
Mahākāśyapa replied: "Good son!
Form has no coming or going; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness likewise have no coming or going."

Within the state of meditative concentration, one manifests the signs of coming and going; however, if one abides in the concentrated mind, all forms are no longer perceived. Because forms are not seen, one is unable to perceive those signs of coming and going.
"Good son! If one abides in a concentrated mind, one immediately attains the dharma-gate of ultimate meaning.
Furthermore, good son!"
"Have you Bodhisattvas been here for long? Viśvabhāṣa-garbha replied,
"The length of time I have been here is equal to the time it took you, Venerable One, to attain the realization of the exhaustion of outflows and the liberation of mind."
Mahākāśyapa said:
"How rare is this Great Being!
You have attained great supernormal powers."
Samantaprabhāgarbha said:
"As for you, Venerable One, who have attained liberation of mind—how long has that been?
Mahākāśyapa replied:
"It has been liberated for a long time.
Samantāloka-garbha said:
"Venerable sir, since you have attained liberation of the mind, in what sense do you designate it as 'mind'?"
Mahākāśyapa said:
"O son of good family!
How do you explain it?"
Vairocanagarbha said,
"If the mind is bound by something, how can it be called liberated?
Mahākāśyapa replied:
"If it is so, O son of good family!
To have fetters within the mind is not called liberation, nor is it called the knowledge and vision of liberation.
Vyapracittigarbha said:
"Venerable Mahākāśyapa!
Since the mind is fundamentally unbound, what is there to liberate?
Mahākāśyapa replied:
"If one understands non-binding as it truly is, that is itself liberation.
Samantaprabhāgarbha said:
"Venerable Mahākāśyapa!"
By means of what mind does one comprehend?
Is it the past, the future, or the present?
If it is the past mind, that has already ceased and perished.
If it is a future mind, it has not yet arrived;
if it is a present mind, it does not abide even now.
Apart from these three periods of time, by what mind could one possibly cognize?
Mahākāśyapa said:
"Good son! The place where mental phenomena cease is not a constituent part of that mind."
Samantaprabhāgarbha said:
"Venerable Mahākāśyapa!
Is it possible to know the very place where this mind ceases?"
Mahākāśyapa said:
"If the mind has ceased, one cannot know.
Vyāpaka-kośa said:
"All those dharmas are extinguished just as the mind is extinguished; therefore, they cannot be cognized.
Mahākāśyapa said, "O son of good family!
"One who has attained great eloquence can answer whatever is asked;
I, however, do not now possess such eloquence.
Viśvabhujagarbha said:
“Venerable Mahākāśyapa!
What do you think?
Regarding all eloquence—whether seen or heard—is there anything that can be attained?”
Mahākāśyapa said:
"There is neither attainment nor hearing. Why is this?"
"Because their nature is dependently originated.
Vairocanagarbha said,
"Is it not the case that all phenomena are likewise so?"
Mahākāśyapa said: "Good son!
All dharmas are also like this!"
Samantaprabhāgarbha said:
"Venerable Mahākāśyapa,
what do you think?"
"If one sees or hears it, can its eloquence ever be interrupted?
Mahākāśyapa replied,
"It is neither destroyed nor interrupted."
The All-Illuminating Treasury said:
"Venerable Mahākāśyapa! So it is, so it is!"
The eloquence of a bodhisattva is never interrupted or destroyed regardless of what is asked.
Kāśyapa, you should know that even if bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were to spend eons answering questions as they arise, their eloquence would still never be interrupted or destroyed.

At that time, when the Bodhisattva Samantāloka-garbha and the Venerable Mahākāśyapa spoke this Dharma, five hundred thousand sentient beings all resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and two hundred bodhisattvas attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).
At that time, the Venerable Mahākāśyapa addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

We entreat the World-Honored One to preach the Dharma as is appropriate for the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī and this great assembly, so that they may obtain great benefit and happiness throughout the long night, and be able to definitively realize the nature of all phenomena!”
At that time, there was a bodhisattva named Prajñākūṭa who, rising from his seat within the great assembly, addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying: "Mañjuśrī!..."
"How is it that the Venerable Mahākāśyapa is able to skillfully proclaim diligence regarding the Dharma?
Mañjuśrī replied, "O Mahākāśyapa!"
"You have already attained fearlessness within the teachings of the śrāvakas.
Bodhisattva Prajñākūṭa said:
"O Mahākāśyapa!..."
"Why do you not abide within the Mahāyāna Dharma?
Mañjuśrī replied,
"O son of good family!"
"O Mahākāśyapa!
It is not that he is unable to abide in the Mahāyāna Dharma; rather, it is because he has attained liberation within the Śrāvaka Dharma.
Bodhisattva Prajñākūṭa said:
“Mañjuśrī, what is called the Dharma of the Śrāvakas?
Mañjuśrī replied:
“World-Honored One, Tathāgata Śākyamuni!
In this Sahā world, you preach the Dharma of the Three Vehicles for the sake of all sentient beings.
What are these three?
What are called the Śrāvaka-yāna, the Pratyekabuddha-yāna, and the Mahāyāna are termed the "Three Vehicles. Why is this?
Because there are sentient beings who give rise to inferior diligence in seeking liberation; therefore, the Buddha skillfully reveals the Three Vehicles as a provisional teaching.
The Bodhisattva Prajñākūṭa said:
"Mañjuśrī, how does the Tathāgata extensively expound the immeasurable gates of liberation: the gate of emptiness, the gate of signlessness, and the gate of wishlessness?"
Mañjuśrī said: "Noble son!
The Tathāgata, through skillful means, has proclaimed immeasurable gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—so that all sentient beings may practice according to the truth."

At that time, while the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī was expounding this Dharma for the Bodhisattva Ratnakūṭa, all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and others in the assembly immediately joined their palms in reverence and,
with one voice, spoke these verses: “With every kind of offering, With precious robes, precious vessels, and manifold ornaments—
To the body adorned by the Honored One Mañjuśrī, We now praise the mass of his merit.”
At that time, the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
At which Buddha-World-Honored One did this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī first resolve his mind upon awakening?”
The Buddha addressed the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu, saying:

"You should now know that in the past, beyond as many eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, there was a world named Golden Flame Radiance. A Buddha appeared in the world there, titled Vimalasūryajvālāprabha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān—fully endowed with these ten epithets."
"O Son of Heaven!
The lifespan of that Buddha was nine hundred and ninety million koṭi-nayuta in number. For the sake of all sentient beings, he taught the Dharma of the three vehicles, namely:
the Śrāvaka vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, and the Bodhisattva vehicle."

At that time, during the Tathāgata’s first assembly for preaching the Dharma, eight hundred and forty million *koṭī-nayuta* of sentient beings dwelt in the Śrāvaka vehicle and attained arhatship; their outflows were exhausted, they had laid down their heavy burdens, they had attained great benefit, all fetters of existence were completely severed, and through right knowledge, their minds were unimpeded and well-liberated.
During his second assembly for preaching the Dharma, seventy million *koṭī-nayuta* of bhikṣus attained arhatship.
During his third assembly for preaching the Dharma, six hundred and fifty million *koṭī-nayuta* of bhikṣus attained arhatship.
Within that Buddha-dharma, there are two groups: the assembly of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās;
and the second group, the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

All those bodhisattvas are non-retrogressive; they have all realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), universally entered boundless gates of samādhi, perfected wholesome dharmas, and further attained boundless gates of dhāraṇī. The Tathāgata has preached for them the Dharma-wheel of non-retrogression, let alone those who have first resolved their minds toward the Great Vehicle, whose number is immeasurable, and among whom there are also immeasurable sentient beings dwelling as pratyekabuddhas.
“Devaputra! That Tathāgata Vimalasūryajvālāprabha universally gathers in sentient beings through immeasurable and innumerable practices of corresponding dharmas.”

At that time, the world-system of Golden Flame Radiance was largely adorned with gold; its various pavilions and halls had pillars made of all kinds of jewels, and all its groves were magnificently embellished with treasures. From within those trees issued sublime sounds, praising the profound and inconceivable Dharma.
That is to say:
the sound of emptiness, the sound of signlessness, the sound of wishlessness;
the sound of lack of intrinsic nature, the sound of non-attachment;
There issued forth sounds of non-arising and sounds of non-origination—such sounds praising all phenomena as these.
All sentient beings who heard these sounds took delight in them.
After that Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma remained in the world for a full one thousand years.
“O Son of Heaven!
At that time, in that world of Golden Flame Radiance, there was a wheel-turning king named Most Excellent Eloquence, who was the sovereign of the four continents.”

At that time, within the buddha-field of the Buddha Vimalasūryajvālāprabha, that king made offerings of food, drink, clothing, bedding, banners, pennants, precious parasols, and all manner of exquisite ritual implements to that Buddha, as well as to all the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the great assembly of bodhisattvas within that buddha-field.
Thus he made offerings for a full *koṭi* of years, deeply planting roots of goodness in the presence of that Buddha.

At the time when that wheel-turning king planted these roots of goodness, eighty-four thousand sentient beings, as well as three million two hundred thousand queens and their retinues within the royal palace, together resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
“O Son of Heaven!

That most excellent Wheel-Turning Sage King had a thousand sons who first gave rise to faith and understanding within the Śrāvaka Dharma, and later further resolved their minds toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, attaining the realization of the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).”
At that time, that king had a daughter named Mahāmati, who possessed great eloquence and profound faith and understanding.
Then Mahāmati, surrounded by a retinue of seven thousand two hundred palace ladies, approached the presence of the Buddha Vimalasūryajvālāprabha with reverent devotion.
Having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, she and her retinue prostrated themselves with their heads to the ground, paying homage at the feet of that Buddha.
At that time, by virtue of her roots of goodness, the daughter Mahāmati immediately resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Having already resolved his mind, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
I wish to seek the fruit of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; however, I am currently unable to realize that *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* by means of this female form."

I only pray that the World-Honored One will reveal to me: what Dharma-gate should be practiced according to principle so that I may transform this female body into a male form and swiftly realize the fruit of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?
At that time, the Tathāgata Vimalasūryajvālāprabha addressed the Great Wisdom Maiden, saying:
“O virtuous woman!
There is a single dharma which, when fully perfected, enables one to transform this female body and attain the marks of a male.”
What is this one?

It is the arousal of the mind of great bodhicitta, the unequaled mind, the most supreme mind within all the three realms, and even the arousal of a conforming mind toward all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
Furthermore, there is one dharma which, if fully possessed, enables one to transform the female body into the male form.
What is this one dharma?
It is to constantly maintain mindfulness toward all Tathāgatas without ever turning away from them, and to listen to and receive the true Dharma without weariness.
Mahāmati!
Furthermore, there are ten dharmas; if one is fully endowed with them, one will immediately transform the female body into the male form.
What are these ten?
One should fulfill the ten paths of wholesome action, whereby the practice of loving-kindness is accomplished;

furthermore, one should study for a long time without weariness, listen to the Dharma without weariness, and attend upon Dharma masters without weariness. If one can fulfill such qualities as these, one will then transform the female body and attain the marks of a male.
“At that time, when that Buddha was preaching this Dharma, the girl Mahāmati immediately transformed her female body into that of a man before all the retinues who had come with her.”
Thereupon, the youth Mahāmati joined his palms in reverence and stepped forward to address the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
I have now transformed my female body and desire to leave the household life within the Buddha-dharma to uphold the bhikṣu precepts; I pray that the Buddha will accept me."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the youth Mahāmati, saying:
"Welcome, Bhikṣu!

Instantly, Mahāmati’s hair and beard fell away of their own accord and a kāṣāya robe appeared upon his body; he assumed the appearance of a bhikṣu with a dignified and composed demeanor as if he had been ordained for a hundred years, and there in the assembly, he realized the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
At that time, all the sons of that king, having learned of these matters, gave rise to a sense of rare wonder; they entered the Buddha’s assembly and all sought to leave the household life.
The Buddha immediately accepted them and preached the essential Dharma to each according to their needs.
At that time, the Bhikṣu Mahāmati addressed the princes, saying:

"I have now attained the supreme benefit; I shall never again give rise to the views of a Śrāvaka. I am determined to seek the fruit of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and cultivate the practice of great compassion to benefit all sentient beings."

You who have given rise to the mind of a śrāvaka should likewise give rise to the supreme mind of great bodhicitta as I have done, and you should conceive the thought of practicing upon the perfectly correct path.
Then the bhikṣu Mahāmati preached the Dharma to the princes according to their needs, and they all attained non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, the World-Honored One Śākyamuni Buddha addressed the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu, saying:
"In that buddha-field of the Buddha Vimalasūryajvālāprabha, is that most excellent eloquent Wheel-Turning Sage-King, the Great Wisdom Maiden, anyone other than this person?"
He is none other than the present Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī!

As for the thousand youths who were that king’s retinue, they have now attained the fruit of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and currently dwell in the world, preaching the Dharma and transforming sentient beings; they are none other than these thousand Buddhas.
That is to say:
"In the eastern direction:

the Tathāgata Atikrama-caryā, the Tathāgata Anantaprabha, the Tathāgata Samantaprabha, the Tathāgata Śrīpati, the Tathāgata Bhūtalakṣaṇa, the Tathāgata Ratnottama, the Tathāgata Ratnaprabhāsa, the Tathāgata Ratnadhvaja, and the Tathāgata Ratnāvabhāsa."
“In the south:

the Tathāgata Most Exalted, the Tathāgata Great Radiance, the Tathāgata Immeasurable Life, the Tathāgata Immeasurable Sound, the Tathāgata Great Renown, the Tathāgata Boundless Renown, the Tathāgata Jewel Light, the Tathāgata Pure Boundless Life, the Tathāgata Moon Aspect, and the Tathāgata Moonlight.”
“In the western direction:

Tathāgata Vimalaprabha, Tathāgata Viśuddhaprabha, Tathāgata Sūryaprabha, Tathāgata Anantaratnottama, Tathāgata Brahmocca, Tathāgata Suvarṇaprabhāsa, Tathāgata Brahmendrarāja, Tathāgata Nāgendrarāja, Tathāgata Sarvaratnakusumendrarāja, and Tathāgata Śālendrarāja.”
“In the north:

Tathāgata Dṛḍhavikrama, Tathāgata Viraja, Tathāgata Śrīgarbhaprabha, Tathāgata Amitagandhaprabha, Tathāgata Siṃhanādavikrāntarāja, Tathāgata Mahābalavīryasambhava, Tathāgata Merukrama, Tathāgata Mahāratnarāśi, Tathāgata Avivartyacakraprabha, Tathāgata Ratnapadārthaśrī, Tathāgata Samantamahāvairocana, and Tathāgata Vijayalabdha.”
“Such Buddhas, Tathāgatas, under various names, currently reside in the worlds of the ten directions, preaching the Dharma and transforming sentient beings.
The Buddha addressed the Devaputra Sumerukūṭa, saying:

“Regarding what you have asked, this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī first gave rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in the presence of the Buddha Vimalasūryajvālāprabha in that world called Suvarṇajvālāloka.”
The Sutra on the Inconceivable Realm of Supernatural Powers Spoken by the Buddha, Volume Middle;
The Sutra on the Inconceivable Realm of Supernatural Powers Spoken by the Buddha, Volume Lower.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma, Dharma-transmitting Master and Imperially Conferred Purple Robe, Subject Shi Hu, during the Song Dynasty, under imperial decree. The Buddha addressed the Son of Heaven:
"From this point forward, this Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī shall again resolve upon the mind of enlightenment in the presence of seventy-two Ganges-sand numbers of Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones."
In the beginning, there was a Buddha named Śrīnālarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who appeared in the world; it was in the presence of that Buddha that he first resolved upon bodhicitta.
Subsequently, there was a Buddha named Ratnarciracaryāśrī who appeared in the world;
subsequently, there was a Buddha named Padmottaravikurvaṇaśrī who appeared in the world.
After him, there was a buddha named Pure Jewel Auspiciousness who appeared in the world;
after him, there was a buddha named Boundless Jewel Auspiciousness who appeared in the world;
after him, there was a buddha named Great Jewel Auspiciousness who appeared in the world.
After him, there was a buddha named Ākāśapradīpa who appeared in the world;
after him, there was a buddha named Mahādharmanṛpati who appeared in the world;
after him, there was a buddha named Sarvaratnasaṃcaya-sudarśanavarṇa who appeared in the world.
After him, there was a Buddha named Śākyamuni who appeared in the world;
after him, there was a Buddha named Guṇaprabhāsa-vyūha-śrī who appeared in the world;
after him, there was a Buddha named Mahāprabha-śrī who appeared in the world.
After that, there was a buddha named Immeasurable Light Great Adornment who appeared in the world;
after that, there was a buddha named King of the Thousand Voices of the Cloud of Transformations who appeared in the world;
after that, there was a buddha named Auspiciousness of Supreme Sunlight who appeared in the world.
After that, there was a Buddha named Uttaramati who appeared in the world;
after that, there was a Buddha named Citrābhāsaśrīrāja who appeared in the world.

Having thus awakened the mind of enlightenment in the presence of as many Buddha-Bhagavāns as there are grains of sand in seventy-two Ganges Rivers, he further encountered various Buddhas and awakened the mind of enlightenment throughout ninety-one kalpas;
moreover, in the presence of these Tathāgatas—Vahniśikha, Gaṇendra, Vyūhakāra, and Prabhāsa—he likewise awakened the mind of enlightenment and planted all manner of roots of goodness.
“Devaputra!

This Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva was able to resolve upon the mind of enlightenment in the presence of such immeasurable and innumerable Buddha-Bhagavāns; having planted various roots of goodness through vast skillful means, he has even now, in my presence as a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, performed all the works of a Buddha through supernatural transformations.”
At that time, the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If all sentient beings who wish to plant roots of goodness can give rise to a mind of faith and understanding toward this vast and sublime Dharma, and can listen to, receive, read, recite, remember, contemplate, and explain it to others, you should know that such persons have well obtained a human body, well beheld the Buddhas, and well heard the sublime Dharma.”
"World-Honored One, we shall bring benefit to this world and not receive food in vain;
yet, how can sentient beings come to give rise to faith and understanding toward this True Dharma?"
The Buddha addressed the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu, saying:
"You should now inquire about such matters with the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī; he shall explain them to you according to the truth."
At that time, the devaputra Samantakusumaketu addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying:
"How may all sentient beings be able to give rise to faith and understanding toward this true Dharma?"
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva said:
“O Son of Heaven!
There is no dharma that can give rise to faith and understanding, for all those dharmas are empty of intrinsic nature and are without arising.”
"If all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature and unarisen, in what, then, could one possibly give rise to faith and understanding?
The Devaputra Samantakusumaketu again addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying,
"We pray that you will briefly explain for us the dharma of the bodhisattva practices."
Mañjuśrī said: "O Son of Heaven, you should know that non-practice is the bodhisattva practice;
furthermore, all phenomena are the bodhisattva practice."
The devaputra Samantakusumaketu asked,
"In what way are all phenomena the bodhisattva practice?
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva replied:
“Son of Heaven, you should know that what is called ‘all dharmas’ refers to:
the four foundations of mindfulness, the eightfold noble path, the five faculties, the five powers, and the seven factors of enlightenment.”
These are briefly described as the practices of a bodhisattva; were they explained in detail, their number would be immeasurable.
If all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain these dharmas, this is precisely what is called the true practice of a bodhisattva.
The devaputra Samantakusumaketu addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying:
"What are called the four foundations of mindfulness?
Mañjuśrī replied:
“O Son of Heaven!

If a bodhisattva contemplates the body as being like space, not apprehending the characteristics of the body, and abides in the dharma of equality, this is called the application of mindfulness to the body within the body;

if a bodhisattva contemplates all phenomena of sensation, finding them unapprehendable internally, externally, or in between, because they are entirely empty, this is called the application of mindfulness to the contemplation of sensation.”

If a bodhisattva contemplates the mind as it truly is, and within its name no form can be seen, such that the characteristics of the contemplated mind cannot be apprehended, this is called the application of mindfulness to the mind within the mind (*cittānupaśyanā-smṛtyupasthāna*).

If a bodhisattva understands as they truly are all those phenomena—that whether wholesome or unwholesome, their intrinsic nature is empty—this is called the application of mindfulness to phenomena within phenomena (*dharmānupaśyanā-smṛtyupasthāna*).
“O Son of Heaven!
These are called the dharmas of the four foundations of mindfulness.
Furthermore, the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying:
"What is called the Dharma of the Eightfold Noble Path?
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva replied:

"If a bodhisattva contemplates all phenomena as being beyond the characteristics of objective spheres, non-dual, without discrimination, and such that not even the slightest phenomenon can be grasped—this is called Right View."

If a bodhisattva contemplates all phenomena, free from all conceptualization and doubt, and accords with right practice that is itself non-contemplative, this is called right intention (*samyak-saṃkalpa*).
If a bodhisattva contemplates the true nature of all phenomena as being neither finite nor infinite, entirely equal, and proclaims them as they truly are, this is called right speech (*samyag-vāc*).

If a bodhisattva contemplates all phenomena as being devoid of the nature of action and ungraspable—whether as something produced or not produced—all of which are entirely equal, and abides in the meaning of reality as it is, this is called right action (*samyak-karmānta*).

If a bodhisattva knows that all phenomena are fundamentally non-continuous, and thus has neither anger nor joy toward them, nor any attachment, abiding in the true and equal Dharma, this is called right livelihood;
if a bodhisattva realizes that all phenomena are without activity and free from various marks, and accords with reality in their diligent practice, this is called right effort;

if a bodhisattva does not give rise to any thoughts regarding all phenomena, understands that the intrinsic nature of all karmas is pure, and dwells in non-conceptuality, this is called right mindfulness.

If a bodhisattva enters into the equality of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena, completely distances himself from the characteristics of objects of perception, and ultimately observes them as being unapprehendable, this is called right concentration.
“O Son of Heaven!
These are called the dharmas of the Eightfold Noble Path.
Furthermore, the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying:
“What are called the five faculties? Mañjuśrī replied:

“If a bodhisattva realizes that all phenomena are fundamentally unarisen, that their intrinsic nature is true reality without advance or retreat, and possesses faith and understanding as it truly is within the state of equality—this is called the faculty of faith;”

If a bodhisattva has no attachment or delight toward any phenomena, remains free from notions of distance or proximity, and abides in true reality, this is called the faculty of diligence (*vīryendriya*).

If a bodhisattva does not direct the mind toward any phenomena, remains detached from various natures through the characteristics of the objects of perception, and because of this detachment from nature, no discursive thoughts arise, this is called the faculty of mindfulness (*smṛtīndriya*).
If a bodhisattva, regarding all phenomena, has nothing to recollect and nothing to apprehend, and is in accord with right concentration, this is called the faculty of concentration (*samādhīndriya*).

If a bodhisattva, regarding all phenomena, is free from the marks of arising and non-arising, and contemplates with precision that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty, this is called the faculty of wisdom.
“O Son of Heaven!
These are called the five faculties.
Furthermore, the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying:
"What is meant by the 'five powers'? Mañjuśrī replied,
"If a bodhisattva does not give rise to various false conceptualizations regarding all phenomena, this is called the power of faith."
If a bodhisattva is able to inquire about the ultimate reality (*paramārtha*) of all phenomena as it truly is, this is called the power of diligence;
if a bodhisattva is free from all lapses of mindfulness regarding all phenomena and remains endowed with right mindfulness, this is called the power of mindfulness;
if a bodhisattva’s mind never grows weary of supramundane phenomena, this is called the power of concentration.
If a bodhisattva possesses unshakable pure faith in the retribution of all karmic actions, this is called the power of wisdom.
O Devaputra!
These are what are known as the five powers.
Furthermore, the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying:
“What is meant by the ‘seven factors of enlightenment’? Mañjuśrī replied:
"If a bodhisattva realizes that all practices are fundamentally unarisen and contemplates the true nature within the dharma of joy, this is called the awakening factor of joy;
if a bodhisattva has no mind of attachment toward any phenomena and contemplates the non-apprehensibility of the characteristics of objects, this is called the awakening factor of pliancy;
if a bodhisattva perceives that the self-nature of all phenomena is without thought and without volitional activity, this is called the awakening factor of mindfulness."

If a bodhisattva seeks the various characteristics of all phenomena and finds them utterly unobtainable, yet records that all wholesome dharmas arise in accordance with reality, this is called the awakening factor of discrimination of phenomena (*dharmapravicaya-saṃbodhyaṅga*).
If a bodhisattva contemplates the nature of the three realms and does not grasp at the characteristics of the three realms, this is called the awakening factor of diligence (*vīrya-saṃbodhyaṅga*).
If a bodhisattva contemplates the mind as unobtainable and consequently has no further realization of any phenomena, this is called the awakening factor of concentration (*samādhi-saṃbodhyaṅga*).

If a bodhisattva knows that all phenomena are fundamentally without basis and thus have no place to abide, and further, that they neither arise nor are perceived, then all phenomena are without object of observation and cannot be apprehended; abiding in equanimity, this is called the awakening factor of equanimity (*upekṣā-saṃbodhyaṅga*).
“Devaputra!
These are called the factors of the seven limbs of enlightenment.
Thus, in brief, are the four foundations of mindfulness, the eightfold noble path, the five faculties, the five powers, and the factors of the seven limbs of enlightenment.”
These Dharma gates, when practiced by Bodhisattvas, constitute the Bodhisattva path;

when practiced by Śrāvakas, they constitute the Śrāvaka path. Should any pure-practicing Brahmins be able to cultivate them, they will immediately attain liberation from all fetters of enmity, eliminate thorns, and pacify all afflictions; they will remain far removed from the suffering of illness, give rise to no fear, turn toward the Buddha-way, and abide in the lineage of the Buddhas.

If any learned sons of the Buddha among the śramaṇas practice these Dharmas, they will immediately transcend saṃsāra and reach the other shore; free from all dust and defilement, they will attain the formless body, cast off their heavy burdens, reach the state of fearlessness, and obtain great bliss.

If bodhisattvas, regarding this Dharma-gate, have contemplated it as it truly is and practiced it according to principle until they have attained fulfillment, these bodhisattvas should receive vast offerings of faithful alms from among gods and humans.
“O Son of Heaven!
For this reason, it is of great benefit for all bodhisattvas to receive food in this world and in every direction without it being in vain.

Furthermore, if you wish to transcend saṃsāra, to shatter the hosts of Māras, to subdue the non-Buddhists, to blow the great dharma-conch, to beat the great dharma-drum, to turn the great wheel of dharma, to raise the great banner of dharma, to liberate all beings from suffering, and to attain great nirvāṇa, you should practice according to the principle within such a sublime and wondrous Dharma-gate.”
“O Son of Heaven!
Regarding the bodhisattva practice you previously asked about, all these dharmas constitute the bodhisattva practice.

When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī was thus teaching this Dharma to the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu, thirty-two thousand devaputras in the assembly, having heard it, attained faith and understanding and dwelt in the equality of dharmas. Immediately, they rained down celestial *mandārava* flowers, *mahāmandārava* flowers, and various wonderful blossoms from the midst of the sky, making offerings to the World-Honored One and the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.
Having made this flower offering, they spoke these words:

"If we, having merely heard this Dharma of the Bodhisattva's practice within the Buddha-dharma for a brief moment, have already obtained such supreme benefit, how much more so for those who are able to listen to this True Dharma with a single-minded focus, give rise to pure faith and understanding, and practice according to the principle! It should be known that such persons are oriented toward the path of the Buddha, possessing spiritual powers like those of Mañjuśrī."
At that time, the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Now, in the final age of the future, you should desire that this True Dharma be widely proclaimed, disseminated, and spread. We only pray that the World-Honored One will [grant this]!”
"I sustain and protect them through my majestic spiritual power.
The Buddha said to the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu, "So it is, so it is."
"The Tathāgatas, the Buddhas, know the time for themselves.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having surveyed the entire assembly, spoke these words:
"O sons of good family!
"Among you in this assembly, who is able to uphold the Buddha’s bodhi and protect and assist the true Dharma for countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of kalpas?
At that time, there were thirty-two koṭis of great bodhisattvas in the assembly, who with one voice and in unison addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“During the Blessed One’s lifetime and after his parinirvāṇa, we shall, through the Buddha’s spiritual power, be able to uphold the Buddha’s bodhi and protect and assist the True Dharma.
Furthermore, in the assembly there was a son of Brahmā named Viśeṣacintin, who rose from his seat, approached the Buddha, and addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

By what accumulation of merit must the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate and fulfill themselves, so that they may receive, uphold, read, recite, explain to others, and widely disseminate this profound true Dharma?
The Buddha addressed the Brahma-son Viśeṣacintin, saying:

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, regarding all the ten powers of the Buddha Tathāgata, cultivates them with complete vigor and firm resolve, and realizes the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti), you should know that such a person is able to uphold the Buddha’s bodhi and protect and assist the True Dharma.”
At that time, the Brahma-son Viśeṣacintin again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has taught, regarding this inconceivable realm of the True Dharma, if there is anyone who hears it and cannot give rise to pure faith and understanding, I know that such a person is not a Mahāsattva and is not in accord with the gateway of the True Dharma; for this reason, World-Honored One, you have not bestowed a prediction of enlightenment upon them.”
The Buddha said, “Son of Brahmā!
It is as you have said; it is so, it is so.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, returning from a world-system in another direction, together with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Now, regarding this True Dharma, during the final five hundred years, we only pray that the World-Honored One will, through his majestic spiritual power, sustain and protect it, so that the True Dharma may spread widely throughout the world, bringing benefit, peace, and happiness to all sentient beings, while the hosts of Māras, wishing to cause its destruction, find no opportunity to do so.

At that time, because the World-Honored One desired to empower and protect this True Dharma, he repeatedly surveyed the entire assembly on his left and right. Immediately, all Buddha-fields in the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, shook in six ways. Then, those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones currently dwelling and preaching the Dharma in the ten directions—numbering as many as the sands of the Ganges—having understood this matter, each likewise used their own spiritual power to empower and protect this Dharma-gate.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"It is rare, World-Honored One!
This profound and inconceivable realm of the True Dharma is sustained by the supernatural power and majesty of the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas."
“World-Honored One!

In the future final age, in whatever cities, towns, or villages there may be, if there are good men who extensively expound this True Dharma for others, I shall go with my retinue to the place where that Dharma-preacher dwells and secretly protect him, causing him to be diligent, to occupy the lion seat with courage and fearlessness, and not allowing any māras to find an opportunity to harm him.”
"I shall now further provide protection by means of this secret vidyā-mantra.
He then spoke the mantra, saying:
*tadyathā | uche | muce | sumuce | pramardini | vyañjani | saṃvyañjani | vārṣaśātani | medatravati mamotre* || "World-Honored One! [he said.]

In whatever places there may be Dharma-preachers, I shall, at their left and right, secretly recite this vidyā and form the Vajradhara mudrā to provide protection, so that the True Dharma may circulate widely.

At that time, among the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, there was a son of the gods named Upapāduka. Not long after his birth in heaven, he came to this assembly of the Buddha, remaining in the midst of the sky. Having heard the true Dharma and witnessed a rare event, he immediately rained down various wondrous flowers such as *māndārava* and *mahāmāndārava*, as well as vast and exquisite precious jewels, as offerings to the World-Honored One, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, and the Dharma being taught.

Having performed these various offerings, he descended from the sky, circumambulated the Buddha three times, and prostrated with his head at the feet of the World-Honored One. Holding a pearl necklace five hundred cubits in length, adorned with every kind of exquisite jewel, he presented it to the World-Honored One and spoke these words:
"How rare, O World-Honored One!"

This vast and profound True Dharma will be able to bring great benefit to sentient beings in the future final age. If there are good men and others who receive and uphold this Dharma in cities, towns, villages, or any other locations, you should know that such persons are born from the Buddha; they uphold the Buddha’s Bodhi and turn the Great Wheel of Dharma.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the devaputra Upāli, saying:
"It is as you have said; it is so, it is so.

If, in the future final age, there should be a son of good family who is able to uphold this Dharma in cities, villages, or any other places, I declare that such a person is born from the Buddha, upholds the Bodhi of the Buddha, and turns the Great Wheel of Dharma."
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī, saying:
"You should receive and uphold this True Dharma of the inconceivable realm."
He further addressed them, saying:

"You should receive and uphold this True Dharma of the inconceivable realm; in the future final age, you must cause it to be widely disseminated so that it does not perish, thereby enabling all sentient beings to attain great benefit and happiness."
The Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I shall uphold the Buddha’s instructions as you have taught; I shall uphold the Buddha’s instructions as you have taught.”

Whether the Buddha remains in the world or has entered parinirvāṇa, during the five hundred years that the True Dharma abides, and even until the final time when the Dharma is about to perish, I shall, through the power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment, protect, assist, proclaim, and disseminate it.

If there are sons of good family or others who expound this True Dharma for the sake of others, I shall go to those persons, concealing my physical form so as not to appear, and listen to the True Dharma they preach; thus I shall rejoice and successively praise it.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
"You should receive and uphold this Dharma-gate of the True Dharma, and widely proclaim and expound it for others."

Ānanda! If any sentient beings receive, uphold, read, or recite even a single four-line verse of this true Dharma-gate, you should know that such persons will certainly achieve the fruit of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and will always be observed by all Buddhas.

Ānanda! Even if someone were to fill all the buddha-fields of the ten directions with precious jewels and offer them as alms to the Buddhas, the mass of merit obtained thereby would not equal that of someone who conceives pure faith in this True Dharma and listens to, receives, reads, and recites it; for this mass of merit is immeasurable and boundless.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the name of this sutra?”
"How should I receive and uphold it?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"This sutra is titled 'The True Dharma of the Inconceivable Realm,' and it is also titled 'The Questions of the Devaputra Samantakusumaketu.'"
It is also titled "The Playful Supernatural Powers of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī";
it is also titled "The Secret Dharma Seal of the Tathāgata";
it is also titled "The Dharma Gate of Non-Retrogression"—thus should it be upheld.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, Mañjuśrī and the other great bodhisattvas, as well as the Devaputra Puṣpadhvaja, and the entire assembly—including gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas—having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Inconceivable Realm of Supernatural Powers of the Mahayana, Scroll II.
